text:
Disappointing decline in quality

I’ve been using Oddbox for a few weeks now and have received around 4–5 boxes. The first couple were genuinely fantastic. Large, fresh apples, lovely potatoes, great-quality fruit and vegetables. My son particularly loved the blueberries, saying they were far better than the supermarket ones.

I was so impressed initially that I even recommended Oddbox to my mum, who went on to order a box herself.

Unfortunately, the quality of my last two deliveries has been a real disappointment.

I’ve had to throw away fruit and vegetables because they were rotten, badly bruised or simply not fit to eat. My most recent box contained one large potato and three tiny ones, with the largest having an actual hole where it had rotted away. The apples were bruised, and the carrots were already looking tired and starting to go soft.

I completely understand the concept behind Oddbox. I actually love the idea of rescuing perfectly edible fruit and vegetables that might otherwise go to waste because they don’t meet supermarket cosmetic standards. That’s precisely what attracted me to the service in the first place.

However, there’s a big difference between receiving imperfect-looking produce and receiving produce that’s already deteriorating or inedible.

I also think the pricing deserves some consideration. I was paying around £27–£28 per box, and when you compare that with specialist organic fruit and vegetable suppliers, there’s surprisingly little difference in price. I’m not suggesting Oddbox is organic, but for a similar amount of money, I can source better-quality produce elsewhere.

The late-night delivery was convenient, and I really wanted this to be a service I continued using. But ultimately, the quality needs to justify the price.

It’s particularly disappointing because the first few boxes were so good. I genuinely thought I’d found a great alternative to supermarket shopping, but the inconsistency in quality has put me off continuing.

A brilliant concept, but the quality and value for money need to be more consistent.
title: Disappointing decline in quality

I really wasn’t sure what to expect from buying fruit and vegetables sight unseen, but I liked the ethos behind the company - and I detest the idea of food being wasted simply for being the ‘wrong’ size or shape. The ability to swap items makes it the perfect way to shop for fruit and vegetables - and with no carrying required.
The initial delivery arrived late one evening and proved to be a treasure trove of good things, as has each delivery since.
My only gripe is about the ‘add on’ items - often fairly heavy jars, which are delivered in the same box with easily squashed items. The tomatoes, pears and blueberries in my first delivery were all ruined by a large jar of chickpeas that was sitting right on top of them. I am trying again this week in the hope it was a one-off but if the fruit and vegetables are squashed again, I’ll stop ordering the add-on items. If eggs can be delivered separately - maybe heavy items should be too?
The delivery box is substantial and recyclable, but if left flattened in the porch, is collected the following week. It’s a really great idea - love it!
